# Release Notes: v1.0.12

> This file is the source of truth for the GitHub Release body.
> The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release-android.yml`)
> copies this file's contents as the Release body via `body_path`.

A maintenance release. Nothing changes for accounts on today's standard money
tracking; the Android fixes below get the app ready for the server-side
("Option B") money tracking that is not switched on yet.

## Android

- **Money never falls back to the old calculation by mistake** — if the app
  could not read which money-tracking mode your account uses, it assumed the
  standard one. It now shows today's money as unavailable (—) and lifetime
  savings from closed days only, until the mode can be read (#148)
- **Export includes daily money for server-tracked accounts** — the JSON export
  now carries `financialMode`, `dailyFinancials` and `financialSummary`, and the
  CSV gains a `daily_financial_summary` section, matching the web export.
  Unavailable amounts are left out rather than written as 0. Exports for
  standard accounts are unchanged (#151)
- **Updated libraries** — Gradle 9.8.2, Kotlin serialization 1.12,
  navigation-compose 2.10 and Firebase BoM 35.1 (#140)

## Web (already live)

These shipped through Firebase Hosting and need no app update; they are listed
here so this release records everything since v1.0.11.

- **Counts stay right after midnight** — just after the day rolled over on its
  own, a count you removed could briefly reappear until the next sync (#150)
- **Updated libraries** — Firebase JS 13.1, framer-motion 14.7 and
  lucide-react 1.64 (#141)

## Not user-visible

A test proving that a replayed or conflicting server operation leaves lifetime
totals, the day ledger and the receipt untouched (#145).
